patch_description: The current pipeline (Kalman/RTS two-pass smoother + bilateral one-pole damper) reaches 0.72 but residual ripple keeps slope changes at ~20 and false reversals at ~14. The one-pole damper's amplitude response leaks noise near its corner. I replace the final damper with a fixed-λ Whittaker–Henderson polish: minimize ||z − y||² + λ||D₂z||², where a constant λ = clip(25·(σ_r/r_std)², 1, 200) is derived from the robust residual MAD already computed. The second-order difference penalty penalizes curvature (not slope), so linear trends pass unattenuated — zero lag for genuine dynamics — while its flatter passband suppresses ripple more uniformly than a one-pole cascade. The system matrix I + λDᵀD is symmetric positive-definite pentadiagonal, solved with a custom O(n) banded (bandwidth-2) Cholesky factorization, preserving the ~0.05s runtime. The polish is applied to the full-length signal before slicing, protecting the len(y) = n − window_size + 1 contract. Key parameters changed: damper alpha heuristic removed entirely; λ schedule is a deterministic noise-ratio map; RTS Q/4 refinement and dynamics-aware blend retained from the best-scoring configuration.
